clue.text: Wicked kinsmen use boys for making mischief

indicators.note: something wicked has gone astray, so the following letters are twisted out of their order

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Naughty relatives employ young lads to stir up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for playful or dishonest misbehaviour, which is mischief.

clue.text: Fun days Thomson managed but never in this time

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a period so long that the thing never happens

indicators.note: to manage letters is to handle and arrange them, so they are set out afresh

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Thomson organised some fun days but they never happened.
explanation.walkthrough: A month of Sundays is an idiom for an extremely long time, so something happening only after one is effectively never.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an impossibly long stretch, the period during which something will never occur.

clue.text: Recently created town based on old president's initiative

indicators.note: in a down entry, being based on something means sitting above it, so the first part goes on top

blocks.note: something recently created is new
Deal is a seaside town in Kent

explanation.surface: A president's scheme is said to rest on a newly built town.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a small coastal town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Deal was Franklin Roosevelt's 1930s programme of economic recovery, an initiative of a former US president.

clue.text: Boy at good point after smooth services

indicators.note: the rest comes after, so the word for smooth is placed first

blocks.note: a smooth, level surface is even
a son is a boy
G is the abbreviation for good
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A boy is placed at a good spot after things have run smoothly in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, so evensongs are church services.

clue.text: Squint, when the chief looked

definitions.note: used as an adjective, meaning squinting

blocks.note: a boss is a chief
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone squinted while the boss was watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss-eyed is British slang for cross-eyed, having a squint in one or both eyes.

clue.text: Those who speak with utter hesitation at one point

blocks.note: to utter is to say
er is the sound of hesitating
south is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Speakers who hesitate at one moment in their talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayers are people who say things, that is, those who speak.

clue.text: Nick's name's on the club house, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the leading letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Nick's name is written on the clubhouse, chiefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick's' reads as a man's name with a possessive; it is the definition followed by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or groove, which is exactly what a notch is.

clue.text: Portuguese lady hears no disturbance

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman in Portugal enjoys peace and quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Senhora is the Portuguese title and word for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Kiss in this part of the forest?

definitions.text: Kiss in this part of the forest?

blocks.clueFragment: Kiss in this part of the forest?
blocks.note: surface reading: a romantic embrace somewhere among the trees
setter's reading: the slang verb for kissing joined to a phrase meaning 'of the forest' names a person's local area

explanation.walkthrough: To neck is British slang for to kiss, and woods are forest, so the phrase splits into kiss plus 'of the forest'; the whole idiom means one's locality.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means one's own district or local area, a part of the world someone belongs to.

clue.text: State of novel woollen garment

blocks.note: something novel is new
a jersey is a knitted woollen top, a jumper

explanation.surface: Someone describes the condition of a brand-new sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a condition, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty United States, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Metal by empty garage in the shade

indicators.note: an empty thing has had its contents removed, leaving only its outer edges

blocks.note: tin is a metallic element
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Some metal lies beside an empty garage out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the shade' suggests a cool place, but 'shade' is a tint of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of a colour, a faint shade or tint.

clue.text: Observes journalists following man

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second word's letters go after the first

blocks.note: he is the pronoun for a man
eds is short for editors, journalists in charge

explanation.surface: Someone watches reporters trailing after a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed a rule or warning is to observe it, paying attention and obeying.

clue.text: Defensive construction is world's task

blocks.note: the earth is the world
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A grand claim that defending ourselves is the job of the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthwork is a bank or mound of soil built as a fortification, a defensive structure.

clue.text: Offences relating to charges covering lion's replacement

indicators.note: a replacement puts things in different positions, so these letters are rearranged
to cover something is to go around it, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: fees are charges for a service
taken as written

explanation.surface: Charges brought over a swapped lion, as in a zoo scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests criminal charges, fitting 'Offences', but it means fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonies are serious crimes, so they are offences in law.

clue.text: Exist partially for the sake of another

definitions.note: the answer is a noun used in 'on behalf of', meaning for the sake of

blocks.note: to exist is to be
half done is partially done

explanation.surface: To live only half a life for someone else's benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on someone's behalf means acting in their interest or for their sake.

clue.text: Install his tables incorrectly

indicators.note: done incorrectly means put in the wrong way, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to fit someone's furniture, done badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish something is to set it up or install it in a position.

clue.text: Friends' character as retail merchant

blocks.note: first meaning: ... Bing from the sitcom Friends
second meaning: a dealer in supplies, originally candles

explanation.surface: A sitcom character is cast as a shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Chandler Bing is one of the six Friends, and a chandler is a dealer selling candles or ship's provisions.

clue.text: Posh wines spilt: it's not clever

indicators.note: spilt liquid scatters, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spilling expensive wine is a foolish thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwise means lacking good sense or judgment, foolish rather than clever.

clue.text: We led; he prepared to sweet-talk

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked into shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: We took the lead while he got ready to charm someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax or persuade with flattery, exactly what sweet-talking does.

clue.text: Yiddish face

blocks.note: surface reading: the features of a Jewish person
setter's reading: face as in cheek or nerve, named by a word borrowed from Yiddish

explanation.walkthrough: Face can mean impudence, as in 'to have the face to ask'; the answer is the Yiddish loanword for that boldness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yiddish-derived word means shameless audacity or nerve, the same as cheek or face.

clue.text: Reportedly, parrot's lost shape

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: Polly is the traditional name for a pet parrot, and lost means gone

explanation.surface: News has it that someone's pet parrot has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly is the stock name for a parrot in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygon is a flat figure with many straight sides, a geometric shape.

clue.text: To some extent soft or ill-formed

indicators.note: something ill-formed is badly shaped, so the letters need rearranging

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is partly soft or misshapen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sort of is an informal phrase meaning somewhat or partly, to a degree.

clue.text: Appear casual in gown with soft texture

blocks.note: a gown is a dress
down is soft fluffy feathers

explanation.surface: Someone looks relaxed wearing a gown of soft fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress down is to wear informal clothes, so as to look casual.

clue.text: Son embraces Capone in the drawing room

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap arms around, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A son hugs the gangster Capone in the drawing room.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is an elegant reception room in a grand house, much like a drawing room.

clue.text: Live down under

blocks.note: to live is to be
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: An invitation to go and live in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' reads as Australia, but 'down' is wordplay and 'under' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Below and under both mean in a lower position than something.

clue.text: Warble a greeting, when led back

indicators.note: going back means reading the word in the opposite direction

blocks.note: yo is a casual greeting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sings a hello as they are being led back.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches into falsetto, a form of warbling.

clue.text: Finger wagging lecture

blocks.note: first meaning: a reproving gesture, standing for a scolding
second meaning: a stern lecture or reprimand

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one lecture with finger-wagging, but both halves separately name a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a reprimand, which comes with a wagging finger and is a lecture in the scolding sense.

clue.text: Small change for old bikes

blocks.note: first meaning: pennies and farthings, low-value British coins
second meaning: Victorian bicycles with one huge and one tiny wheel

explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny; the bicycle was named for a large and a small coin side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The penny-farthing was the high-wheeled Victorian bicycle, and pennies and farthings were small coins.
